The role comes from a 'role:' scope and defaults to 'agent'. server.ts:187-189 runs verificarTetoMcp, ensureScope(mcp:write) and ensureRole(agent) before the handler. Only an admin outside a support session can create tokens (app/api/v1/settings/api-tokens/route.ts:45-58). local_checks.invariant: Every service-role read and write that crm_set_conversation_sector makes is bound to ctx.organizationId: the sector lookup, the conversation lookup, the setor_membros probe, the UPDATE, fn_conversation_assign and fn_request_channel_routing.
local_checks.result: Holds. The sector list is filtered by organization_id (governance.ts:264-267), and the name or id must match an entry in that list. transferirParaSetor (servico.ts:125-220) filters organization_id on the conversation select, on setores, on setor_membros and on the UPDATE, and passes the org to both RPCs. local_checks.invariant: The new tool must not give an agent-role mcp:write token any authority over private conversations, or over conversations controlled by another attendant, that the same principal did not already have.
local_checks.result: No new authority. The per-attendant gates are by design limited to human sessions. The last fn_conversation_assign in baseline.sql (0499) checks visibility only when auth.uid() is not null, with the comment that server routing without auth.uid() stays the same. exigirControleDaConversa returns early when actor.type !== 'user'. Before this diff, the same agent-role token could already: read any conversation and its full message history, private ones included (crm_get_conversation and crm_get_conversation_history use service role with only an org filter, conversations/_handler.ts:497-526 and messages/_handler.ts:311); transfer or release any owner (crm_assign_conversation, requiresRole agent, present at d823c3914); and silence the bot (crm_request_human_handoff). The sandbox check used Postgres 16 with the baseline and one dummy org. A PRIVATE conversation owned by agent a1 was tested three ways. (A) A human agent a3 as 'authenticated' got select 0 rows, fn_can_view_conversation(2-arg) false, and fn_conversation_assign 0 rows. (B) service_role, the token path, running the pre-existing crm_assign_conversation RPC: release gave owner null and status open; transfer to a2 gave owner a2, status claimed and bot_silenced_until infinity. (C) service_role running the new transferirParaSetor sequence: the UPDATE succeeded, the release returned 1 row, and the final state was setor_id Financeiro, owner null, is_private true, bot_silenced_until infinity. The new tool's effects are a subset of what this principal already had.

local_checks.invariant: No weaker parallel path to the same sector change. Under the tokenRole doctrine in auth-dual, the bearer floor must not be lower than the MCP tool's floor for the same write. The peer root causes must not be re-reported.
local_checks.result: Holds. POST /api/v1/conversations/[id]/setor is cookie-only: it uses requireRole and has no PUBLIC_PATHS entry, so a bearer gets 401 at the proxy. It checks RLS visibility through the session client and exigirControleDaConversa before using the admin client. The MCP tool is therefore the only bearer path, and its floor (agent with mcp:write) applies to it directly. The O7 design doc (fatia 4) describes the tool as the AI's sector handoff using the transferirParaSetor rule. Two related root causes belong to peers and are not reported here: the in-process AI turn not binding conversation_id (ai-turn-tool-conversation-unbound:crm_set_conversation_sector, a different principal, since only the runtime sets ctx.contatoDoTurno or turnContactId), and the invited participant controlling a private conversation through the 2-arg fn_can_view_conversation (fn-can-view-conversation-2arg:participante-controla-conversa-privada).

local_checks.invariant: Does any product-facing statement promise that an agent-role token cannot reassign conversations, which would make the agent-rank floor a broken boundary?
local_checks.result: Partial mismatch, not a boundary failure. The token UI scope catalog (ApiTokensClient.tsx:46-51) labels role:manager as 'needed to create and assign' and says agent-role tokens get 'Role agent insufficient' on assign. But crm_assign_conversation and crm_create_lead have required only agent since the imported baseline, and crm_set_conversation_sector follows the same floor. The label is stale relative to long-standing code. The token is still an admin-issued, org-scoped integration with full read of the org, so no principal gains state it could not already reach. Recorded as hardening.

critic_reason: IN-SCOPE. lib/mcp/tools/governance.ts:251-314 adds crmSetConversationSector with requiresRole "agent" and requiresScope "mcp:write". Its handler calls transferirParaSetor(ctx.supabase, …) with only an organization filter. lib/mcp/tools/index.ts:165 registers the tool in allTools, and lib/mcp/server.ts:56-58 serves allTools over /api/mcp (public-paths.ts:84, bearer allowed) with createAdminClient. transferirParaSetor (lib/setores/servico.ts:125-219, changed) has no is_private, visibility-mode or control check, and it sets soltouDono when the current owner is not in the sector (lines 199-209). The HTTP route for the same effect (conversations/[id]/setor/route.ts:40-67) reads the conversation under RLS and calls exigirControleDaConversa. hunter-ia's unit covered only the AI-turn binding (candidate ai-turn-tool-conversation-unbound), and binding the tool to the turn does not close this human-principal path; the hunter listed this path in uncovered.json. Also check whether an own_and_sector agent (0543) can move other agents' conversations into its own sector and so gain read access.
hardening_notes: The admin token screen (app/app/settings/api-tokens/_components/ApiTokensClient.tsx:46-51) says role:manager is required to assign conversations. In code, an agent-role mcp:write token can transfer or release any org conversation (crm_assign_conversation, pre-existing) and can now move any conversation, private or owned by another attendant, into a sector, which silences the AI and releases the owner (crm_set_conversation_sector). Either correct the label, or give external-bearer calls to conversation-control tools a manager floor. The floor must apply per ingress: the in-process agent runs as ai_operator, rank 3, below manager, so a plain requiresRole: manager would break the native agent. A regression test would call both tools through createMcpServer with an agent-role token and expect -32002.

transferirParaSetor (lib/setores/servico.ts:182-210) writes setor_id and bot_silenced_until=infinity before fn_conversation_assign releases the owner. If that RPC raises (for example support_readonly), the conversation stays silenced and in the sector with its old owner. This is a consistency issue, not a privilege one. Wrapping the steps in one definer function would make it atomic.

local_checks.result: Holds. The route calls requireRole('manager') before any read (route.ts:96). The org comes from the session (authz.org.orgId). local_checks.invariant: Note attachment upload writes only into internal-media under {active org}/{conversation the caller can see}/, with a server-generated object name, and only for agent and above.
local_checks.result: Holds. POST notes/media calls resolveAuthDual with role agent (route.ts:50). The path is not in PUBLIC_PATHS, so the global proxy rejects bearer and only the cookie branch reaches the handler. That branch uses the session client under RLS (auth-dual.ts:148). The conversation is looked up with that client plus an explicit organization_id filter before any write (route.ts:68-75). The server builds the object name as `${org}/${conversationId}/note-${randomUUID()}.${ext}` (route.ts:101), with upsert:false and the bucket fixed to internal-media. No client-controlled path segment reaches storage. validateOutboundMedia gates size (50 MB) and MIME (prefix allowlist).

local_checks.invariant: A note created through the API can only reference an attachment path inside its own organization and conversation, and only in a conversation the caller may see.
local_checks.result: Holds for the API path. POST /notes rejects anexo.storage_path unless isMediaPathOwnedBy(path, org, conversation) passes (route.ts:92). That check requires the prefix `${org}/${conv}/` and caminhoDeMidiaLiteral, which refuses empty, '.' and '..' segments, %, backslash, ?, # and C0/DEL characters (upload-validation.ts:43-48). The insert runs through the session client under RLS conversation_notes_write (baseline.sql:49183-49203). That policy requires agent or above, org membership and the 2-arg fn_can_view_conversation. The conversations RLS also applies inside its EXISTS subquery and carries the is_private, sector and participant rules from 0544. The API refuses cross-tenant and cross-conversation linking.

local_checks.invariant: The signed download is bound to an existing note of a conversation the caller can see in the active org, to the internal-media bucket, to that exact object and to a short TTL.
local_checks.result: Holds. GET notes/[noteId]/media checks the conversation (RLS plus org filter) before the note (route.ts:42-49). It selects the note by id, conversation_id and organization_id (51-57). It re-checks the STORED path with isMediaPathOwnedBy (61) and signs only in internal-media, for 60 s (66-68). storage-js puts the raw path into /object/sign/<bucket>/<path> (index.cjs:1060-1062). The literal check blocks every traversal form except one: a final segment with a trailing space. WHATWG URL parsing strips that space, so `{org}/{conv}/.. ` collapses at most to `{org}/`, which is a folder that cannot be signed and does not leave the tenant. internal-media is private and has no storage.objects policy, so only the service-role route can sign.

local_checks.invariant: A stored note body, MIME type or attachment cannot execute script in another member's app-origin session.
local_checks.result: No app-origin sink. NoteCard renders body and author through React text interpolation. kindFromMime(note.media_mime) picks the component (NoteCard.tsx:31), and the file is used only as an ,

local_checks.invariant: The direct PostgREST path to conversation_notes cannot turn the attachment pointer into a read of another conversation's or tenant's internal-media object.
local_checks.result: The database does not guard pointer writes, unlike messages, which has trg_messages_midia_so_pelo_servidor. Under RLS as authenticated, a non-author agent updated another user's note: it set media_storage_path='x/y/z', changed created_by_name and backdated created_at (UPDATE 1), then deleted the note (DELETE 1). The read boundary still holds. Before signing, the download route re-validates the stored path against the org and conversation in the URL (route.ts:61), so a forged pointer returns 404, not another object. Three residual effects remain: a forged pointer can feed fn_enfileirar_midia_vencida step 2c; it can keep a deleted note's orphan alive; and the route and RLS disagree on authorship and deletion. These need knowledge of the target path or are access-control questions, so they are recorded under hardening and uncovered.

hardening_notes: The note upload (app/api/v1/conversations/[id]/notes/media/route.ts:91-105) stores the browser-declared file.type verbatim as the object's Content-Type. validateOutboundMedia only checks the part before ';' with startsWith, so image/svg+xml passes, and so do comma-joined values such as 'image/png, text/html'. The content renders on the Supabase Storage origin via the 302, not on the app origin, so this is not a session finding. Fix: sniff the bytes server-side, store a canonical MIME type from a closed list, and serve non-image types with Content-Disposition: attachment.

conversation_notes has no database guard on media_storage_path, media_mime, media_size_bytes or created_at (messages has trg_messages_midia_so_pelo_servidor). Through PostgREST, an agent can bypass isMediaPathOwnedBy (observed in notes-rest-probe.txt). The download route's re-check prevents reads from other conversations. Two effects remain. A forged same-org path with a backdated created_at is enqueued by fn_enfileirar_midia_vencida step 2c and removed by the service-role drain; this needs the target object's name. A forged reference also keeps a deleted note's attachment out of the orphan sweep. Fix: add a CHECK constraint or trigger that binds media_storage_path to organization_id||'/'||conversation_id||'/note-%', and revoke UPDATE on the media and authorship columns from authenticated.

NoteCard picks the renderer and the label from anexo.media_mime and media_size_bytes, which POST /notes stores from the request (lib/schemas/notes.ts accepts any string and any integer). These values are not tied to the uploaded object, although the 0547 column comment says media_mime is the validated stored MIME type. Derive them from the object, or from a server-issued upload receipt, instead of the request body.

caminhoDeMidiaLiteral (lib/messaging/media/upload-validation.ts:43-48) accepts a trailing space. WHATWG URL parsing strips it inside createSignedUrl, so '{org}/{conv}/.. ' resolves to '{org}/'. This is harmless today because it cannot leave the org, but it should reject trailing spaces as isMediaPathInOrganization does.

Retention step 1 (baseline.sql:47641) only expires messages that have media_storage_path. Messages whose persistence never completed (failed or never requested) keep media_url past media_retention_days, and GET /api/v1/messages/[id]/media keeps proxying them from the provider. Fix: null media_url and mark these rows expired too.

Conversation unification (baseline.sql:13795) moves conversation_notes to the winning conversation, but media_storage_path still points to the losing conversation's folder. The download route's ownership check then returns 404 for those attachments. This affects availability only.

The 0547 LGPD trigger enqueues note attachments with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. If a path's queue row is already in the terminal 'failed' state, a later anonymization does not reopen it. Fix: use the do-update-where-terminal pattern that fn_enfileirar_midia_vencida uses.

local_checks.invariant: An invited participant (agent) gets read and reply only. It must not get control (close, change sector or owner, start a chatbot, change privacy) over a conversation it had no access to before the invite, including a private conversation of another agent.
local_checks.result: Violated. exigirControleDaConversa calls the 2-argument fn_can_view_conversation, which has no is_private term. In visibility_mode 'all' it returns true for any agent. The routes that use it (POST close, POST setor, POST chatbot, PATCH status) first read the conversation with the session client, and the 0544 participant branch makes the private conversation visible to the invitee. So the invitee passes the gate. The probe ran in a throwaway Postgres with baseline.sql installed, in an org with mode 'all' and a private conversation owned by DONO. Before the invite the invitee sees 0 rows and can update 0 rows. After the invite: the gate RPC with 2 args returns true; the 3-argument privacy rule (used by fn_conversation_assign) returns false; direct UPDATE is_private=false affects 1 row, and a colleague who was never invited then sees the conversation and its message (0 -> 1); UPDATE assigned_to_user_id=self affects 1 row and the original owner then sees 0; UPDATE status='closed' affects 1 row; the sector route's service-role release (fn_conversation_assign without auth.uid()) affects 1 row and the owner then sees 0 while the invitee still sees 1. Control case: in mode 'own' the gate returns false and the update affects 0 rows.

local_checks.invariant: Only the conversation owner or a manager+ can invite or remove colleagues. The invitee must be an active non-viewer member of the same org. The list read follows conversation visibility.
local_checks.result: Holds. POST and DELETE require agent+. They load the conversation with the admin client filtered by the org taken from the cookie, and call requireRole('manager') when the caller is not assigned_to_user_id. The invitee is checked against user_organizations (same org, revoked_at null, role != viewer). DELETE of a different user_id requires owner or manager; leaving yourself is always allowed. GET reads the conversation with the session client (RLS) before listing participants with the admin client filtered by org and conversation. The table is server-only (revoke all from authenticated; select of your own row only).

local_checks.invariant: Sector membership (which grants own_and_sector visibility) is writable only by manager+ of the same org.
local_checks.result: Holds. The routes require manager. membrosRecusados checks active non-viewer members of the same org. RLS on setores and setor_membros allows insert, update and delete only to fn_role_at_least(org,'manager'). Grants are revoked first, then enumerated, so there is no TRUNCATE.

local_checks.invariant: Sibling control routes (transfer, claim, privacy) do not grant control through the participant or sector branch.
local_checks.result: Holds at the route layer. Transfer and claim go through fn_conversation_assign with the session client. Its last definition (baseline.sql 43048) applies the 3-argument privacy-aware rule when auth.uid() is set, so the invitee is refused (probe P2d: 0 rows). The privacy route requires manager or assigned_to_user_id == caller. The weaker path is the shared 2-argument gate and the RLS restrictive policies, recorded in the candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Sector routing hands a conversation only to active members of that sector, and only inside the sector's hours.
local_checks.result: Holds. Routing intersects the channel responsibles with setor_membros, filters to unrevoked agent/manager/admin members, and returns an empty list outside the sector's horario. horario has a jsonb object CHECK and is parsed with Zod. There is no authorization effect beyond routing.

hardening_notes: An invite is not ended when the conversation is later made private (privacy route) or transferred: earlier conversation_participants rows keep read and reply. That is consistent with the documented intent, but the owner is not prompted. Consider showing or ending active invites in the privacy and transfer flows.

lib/notifications/web_push.ts podeVerConversa does not model own_and_sector or conversation participants. Sector colleagues and invitees miss pushes for conversations they can read (under-notification only, no disclosure).

local_checks.result: Disagreement confirmed. conversations_select (baseline 51236) and fn_conversation_assign (43091) use fn_can_view_conversation(org, assigned, is_private). The 0544 restrictive policies conversation_participant_read_is_not_control_update/delete (51259) and message_participant_reply_is_not_history_update/delete (51271, 51286), plus exigirControleDaConversa, use the 2-argument form, which ignores is_private. The shipped invariant tests seed only visibility_mode 'own' (test lines 102 and 104), the one mode where the two rules agree. The local probe in mode 'all' shows the invitee gaining UPDATE on assigned_to_user_id, is_private and status of a private conversation. The message-history variant was traced in source only and not run locally: in mode 'all', the restrictive message UPDATE and DELETE policies let the invitee rewrite or delete the owner's outbound 'user'/'crm' messages. The column trigger fn_mensagem_colunas_de_envio allows body changes on those rows.

local_checks.invariant: The sector read branch only widens agent reads in own_and_sector orgs, never exposes private conversations, never crosses org, and grants no write.
local_checks.result: Holds. fn_escopo_de_setor_da_conversa (security definer, revoked from public and anon) returns rows only for setor_membros of auth.uid() whose live role is 'agent' and whose org mode is own_and_sector. The policy branch requires setor_id not null and not is_private, and matches on (organization_id, setor_id). For writes, the 2-argument rule returns false for agents in own_and_sector unless they own the conversation, so sector colleagues cannot pass the restrictive UPDATE policy or the route gate.

local_checks.invariant: Removal of an invite, membership revocation, or sector removal stops future reads and does not leave stale grants.
local_checks.result: Holds for the stated lifecycle. The participant branch requires left_at is null and is evaluated live. The DELETE route sets left_at. Membership revocation removes reads (enforced by the existing invariant). Sector membership and mode are read live inside fn_escopo_de_setor_da_conversa. One note, recorded as hardening: an invite is not ended when the conversation is later made private or transferred.

local_checks.invariant: Derived copies (push notifications carrying contact name and message preview) do not reach users the conversation policy hides.

The value only selects a rate-limit bucket. No authorization decision uses it here, and tenants/provision only buckets failures against a secret of at least 32 chars. Per-request work is linear: one satori render of at most 512 px plus a storage fetch of at most 512 KiB of a logo the caller can already fetch publicly. Redis keys expire after 60 s, and the in-memory fallback is swept (rate-limit.ts:79-101,125-145). local_checks.invariant: Other source-visible bounds limit how many ceiling-bypassing Jev calls one sender can cause.
local_checks.result: Each ungated call needs all of these: the org opted into the pedidos tasks; a validated typesafe/openrouter credential; a published, unpaused AI agent on the session (haQuemAtendaASessao); conversation eligibility (lib/ai/elegibilidade/gate.ts denies on force_human or silenced conversation); and !isLeadInHandoff (lib/agent-engine/agent/human-handoff.ts:319). Once the ceiling blocks, the agent turn's LlmBudgetExceededError is escorted by comHandoffSeOrcamentoAcabar, which calls performHumanHandoff (lib/agent-engine/agent/inbound-turn.ts, reason HANDOFF_REASON_ORCAMENTO). That sets force_human and bot_silenced_until, which closes both gates for that contact. The drain postpones the turn while that conversation's media is being derived, up to 120 s (lib/agent-engine/edge/crm/drain.ts:221,525). So the bypass is limited to audio a contact sends before its first budget-blocked turn: in practice one or a few calls per new contact, with no persistence. The 'bloquear' verdict itself needs a budget_warning issued earlier in the same month (decidirOrcamento condition 6).

local_checks.invariant: The ceiling bypass causes meaningful operator-owned spend, compared with the minimum ceiling and with the paid work that must precede it.
local_checks.result: I ran costCents('jev-1.13.0', ...) in the sandbox. One call costs 0.00126 cents at 300 input tokens, 0.0042 at 1,000, 0.063 at 15,000 (about an hour of transcript) and 0.21 at 50,000. Reaching 1% of the minimum binding ceiling (PISO_DE_TETO_CENTS = 100) takes 239 typical calls. Each call needs a distinct not-yet-handed-off contact, as the previous check showed. The OpenRouter model id 'typesafe/jev-1.13' is unpriced (cost_cents null). Each such call is preceded by a Whisper transcription of the same audio. That transcription is a far larger per-call cost and is outside every ceiling by declared design (docs/design/teto-de-orcamento.md §6 item 2: 'Gasto multimodal continua fora de qualquer teto'). The ungated Jev call adds negligible spend on top of that declared gap, so this has no concrete shared or operator-spend impact. It is recorded as hardening, not as a finding.
